title: Slash command argument parsing and output shape
cluster_summary: Seven independent per-repo slash nits with no shared root cause and no upstream fix that would make them moot (LibKa0s-Slash only formats rows; each addon parses its own arguments). Only AM-R-05 needs a code fix: a destructive delete can hit the wrong container when a container has a bare-number name. The fix is to copy MultiMeters' WindowManager.Resolve order (name first, then id) and refuse when the two disagree. MM-R-05 is a documented design limit with a working id-based workaround, so it needs a doc line only. KC-R-03 is sanctioned by the standard (slash-commands.md:87, debug-logging.md:344). It and the rest are optional polish to fold in only when the files are already being touched.

verdicts.assessment: Verified: findContainer (settings/Slash.lua:169-170) returns FindContainer(tonumber(arg)) before any name match, while the validator accepts a name like '3'. So '/am delete 3' can delete a different container than the one named '3', and AceDB has no undo. The case is rare, but the result cannot be reversed, and MultiMeters' Resolve already does name-first.
verdicts.remediation: In findContainer, try an exact (case-insensitive) name match first and fall back to the numeric id. If a numeric argument names one container and is the id of a different one, refuse with one new enUS line naming both. Make '#N' always mean an id. Update the precedence note in docs/slash-dispatch.md rows 12 and 14. Add 2-4 cases to tests/test_slash_verbs.lua, and update the badge and docs/test-cases.md in the same commit. Do not forbid numeric names.

verdicts.assessment: Accurate but cosmetic. The standard's table row is illustrative, not mandated wording. The real drift is that docs/slash-dispatch.md:51 describes listing output that the code does not print.
verdicts.remediation: Fix docs/slash-dispatch.md:51 to describe the real listing output ('name  #id - unit - type - style'). The debug-row em dash is an optional value-only edit. If the key text changes, remove the old enUS key in the same change so test_locale stays green.

verdicts.assessment: The behaviour is real but it is a documented design decision (settings/Slash.lua comment above WINDOW_VERBS.copy; docs/slash-dispatch.md:75), not a bug. CopyFrom resolves through M.Resolve, which falls back to tonumber(key), so '/mm window copy 1 Second' already copies a default 'Multi Meters #1' window by its id. Trying every split point is the invented syntax the comment rejects, and it brings ambiguity of its own.
verdicts.remediation: Documentation only: in docs/slash-dispatch.md:75 (and optionally the WINDOW_USAGE text), say that the source may be given as its window id, which covers default names with spaces. Make no parser change.

verdicts.assessment: The mechanics are verified (core/KickCD.lua: refuse(...) then runDebug(self, "") toggles the console). But the standard explicitly sanctions toggling on an unknown debug word (slash-commands.md:87; debug-logging.md:344, 'toggle, or usage'), so this is not a defect. The only nit is that KickCD does both, printing a refusal and also toggling, and the test hides that with a re-toggle.
verdicts.remediation: Optional: choose one sanctioned behaviour. Either refuse and print the sub-verb list without toggling (split the list printer out of the bare branch), or toggle silently. Then pin it in tests/test_slash.lua in place of the 'toggle it back' workaround.

verdicts.assessment: This is a feature request, not a defect. The help text says 'current target', the callees default to 'target', and /kcd diagnostics already covers focus. Won't-fix is defensible.
verdicts.remediation: Only if it lands with KC-R-03 in the same function: parse an optional target|focus word, pass it to DebugDump and DebugInterrupt, and update the two help strings and the tests. Otherwise close it as won't-fix, citing diagnostics coverage.

verdicts.assessment: Accurate and harmless. The virtual 'General' page resolves as a test category and prints a truthful '(no matching strings)'. The only cost is that the Valid list advertises a no-op.
verdicts.remediation: Optional: in runTest, treat a resolved 'General' as unknown and leave it out of the 'Valid:' list. Add one test_slash case, and update the badge and inventory in the same commit.

verdicts.assessment: Verified in statusFlags: the preview branch and Anchor.IsUnlocked() both add an 'unlocked' flag, so the normal unlocked state prints it twice. Cosmetic, and the fix is a one-line guard.
verdicts.remediation: Add the bare 'unlocked' only when NS.Anchor.IsUnlocked() is true and NS.State.preview is false, so the case where setPreview refused still reports the unlock. Add one status-output test.
